name: RSS to Newsletter
headline: RSS to Newsletter - Convert Feeds to Emails
short_description: Convert RSS or Atom feeds into email newsletters. Marketing teams benefit from automated content distribution. Connects to Amazon SES, Mailchimp, and Sendy for email delivery.
author: ElliotKillick

sections.overview:
rss2newsletter automates the conversion of RSS and Atom feeds into formatted email newsletters, eliminating manual content distribution. It integrates with listmonk and Amazon SES to send emails at a fraction of proprietary platform costs. The tool automatically extracts content images using OpenGraph metadata and requires minimal setup—download listmonk, install rss2newsletter via pip, configure a template, and start sending. Built as a lightweight, open-source alternative to Mailchimp's RSS-to-Email feature, it supports feeds from blogs, news sites, and social media. Teams managing content distribution, newsletter publishers, and cost-conscious marketers benefit from its simplicity and affordability.
Automated blog post distribution to subscriber email lists
Publishing curated news feeds as branded newsletters
Cost-effective alternative to Mailchimp for RSS-based campaigns
Lightweight newsletter automation for small teams or personal projects
sections.setup:
No install command available. Check the GitHub repository for manual installation instructions.
`git clone https://github.com/ElliotKillick/rss2newsletter`
sections.usage:
```
Convert the latest 5-10 entries from the RSS feed at [RSS_FEED_URL] into a polished email newsletter. Format it for [EMAIL_PLATFORM: Amazon SES/Mailchimp/Sendy]. Include a subject line, header image from [HEADER_IMAGE_URL], and a 'Read More' CTA button linking back to the original articles. Use a [TONE: professional/casual/fun] voice and keep the length under [MAX_LENGTH: 800 words]. Add a brief introduction paragraph summarizing the key themes in this issue. Ensure all links are tracked with UTM parameters using [SOURCE: newsletter], [MEDIUM: email], and [CAMPAIGN: [NEWSLETTER_NAME]].
```
